text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi stops collection of activity fees, an extra charge on schoolchildren, in primary schools countrywide.
- Four people are arrested in connection with a syndicate illegally issuing the new national identity cards.
- Police Commissioner Duncan Wachira says police should stop harassing unaccompanied women at night.
- A police inspector is shot dead in Machakos after staging a dramatic highway robbery and snatching 120,000 shillings from a motorist.

- A crucial opposition interparty meeting to censure the reappointment of cabinet minister Nicholas Biwott and map out modalities for a single presidential candidate flops after being snubbed by 57 MP's.

- The Nakuru Roman Catholic Diocese claims that the Irish brother shot dead on Tuesday by policemen who had gone to rescue him from a gang of 15 thugs was gunned down because he confronted the provincial administration over corruption over the new generation identity cards.

- Former Langata member of parliament Raila Odinga describes his political rival Michael Kijana Wamalwa, chairman of Opposition party FORD-Kenya, as a calamity hovering over Kenya's political landscape.

- The government instructs the Kenya Revenue Authority to launch special investigations into the sugar industry after receiving reports that thousands of tonnes of imported sugar finds its way illegally into the local market.

- The names of well-heeled Kenyan Asians and their respective patrons in the top tier of Kenya's political establishment are set out by People investigators, along with their role in multi-billion shilling deals.
- Opposition party FORD-Kenya appears about to collapse as the national delegates assemble this weekend to elect national party officials.
- The Electoral Commission has set in motion activities that will culminate in the general election being held sometime late November or early December 1997.
